title: Sophie waits by the canal
body: After dark Sophie walks along the canal, down a sheltered path lit only by lamps from the wharf across the water, where the noise of the city sounds muffled and far away. She sits on a wooden bench beneath a solitary elm, a place where lovers sometimes come, and waits for Danny Casey. At first she pictures him coming out of the shadows and imagines her own excitement. Only after some time does she begin to weigh this against the idea of his not coming. She feels 'the pangs of doubt' and remembers Geoff saying that Casey would never come. The story observes: 'Resignation was no sudden thing.' Sophie thinks that sadness is a hard burden to carry; she already sees the slow walk home and Geoff's disappointed face. Others will doubt her, as they always have, but she tells herself she will hold up her head: 'But we know how it was, Danny and me.' Then she climbs the crumbling steps to the street and, seeing her father's bicycle outside the pub, is glad he will not be at home.
